ui.content:
`Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity` had 11 unresolved merge conflict blocks committed into it. Someone committed the file with the `<<<<<<<` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` markers still in place, which is why Unity can't parse the scene. I removed all the markers. I haven't opened the scene in Unity, so it's untested.

I kept the `HEAD` side of each block and dropped the older side from commit `38aa39f` ("Added simple inv"). `HEAD` is the newer version.

**Player:** this keeps the player's scale at 1 and its CharacterController center at y=-0.2. The dropped side had scale 0.27 and center y=-2.59.
**Shadow caster:** this keeps the shadow-caster settings and shadow data on the `HEAD` side, including its `rid` ids. The dropped side's much larger shadow data went with it.

I checked that the player's child object (`fileID 2023870995`) exists in the file. No markers remain.

If the player's size or collider looks wrong when you open it, that's the dropped older side; I can restore it from `38aa39f`.

`Assets/Settings/UniversalRenderPipelineGlobalSettings.asset` also shows as modified in `git status`. That's most likely Unity rewriting it on import. I left it alone.

Reopen the project and the scene should load. Anyone else who pulled the broken file will need to pull again after you commit and push this fix.

ui.content:
I've ported the colour maze to Unity. When the player picks up the Clue Letter and holds its slot key to inspect it, the maze opens instead of the letter image. Both scripts compile without errors against the project's Unity 6000.6 assemblies, but I haven't played it in the editor yet.

- **New file, `Assets/ClueMinigame.cs`:** a straight port of `minigameOne.js`.
  - Same 10×10 board, rainbow order and starting spot in the centre.
  - Same controls: one step every 90 ms with W/A/S/D, E restarts.
  - Clearing the white tile shows the "Fell, Jerk, Thief" win box.
  - The board is drawn at 5× the sketch's size (70 px per tile instead of 14), so its fractional offsets land on whole pixels.
  - Progress is kept if the player closes the letter and opens it again; only E resets it.
- **Edited, `Assets/InventoryInspection.cs`:** inspecting the item called "Clue Letter" now shows the maze, with the hint `W A S D Move / E Restart / ESC Close`. While the maze is open, W/A/S/D move the puzzle player instead of rotating the item, and Esc closes it.
- **Scene:** the maze component adds itself to the Inventory System object at runtime. I didn't edit the scene file because the Unity editor was open.
- **Pause:** player movement, the camera, pickups and the inventory bar already pause during inspection, so they also pause while the maze is open.

**Missing artwork:** the four border images (`orca.png`, `gazelle.png`, `iguana.png`, `panther.png`) aren't in the repo, so the frame draws black squares, like the sketch does before its images load. To use the real art, add a `ClueMinigame` component to the Inventory System object and assign the four textures in its `borderTiles` field. The sketch's `Map.png` is loaded but never drawn, so I left it out.

I ran a solver on the board layout and it can be finished.

content.text:
I've ported the colour maze to Unity. When the player picks up the Clue Letter and holds its slot key to inspect it, the maze opens instead of the letter image. Both scripts compile without errors against the project's Unity 6000.6 assemblies, but I haven't played it in the editor yet.

- **New file, `Assets/ClueMinigame.cs`:** a straight port of `minigameOne.js`.
  - Same 10×10 board, rainbow order and starting spot in the centre.
  - Same controls: one step every 90 ms with W/A/S/D, E restarts.
  - Clearing the white tile shows the "Fell, Jerk, Thief" win box.
  - The board is drawn at 5× the sketch's size (70 px per tile instead of 14), so its fractional offsets land on whole pixels.
  - Progress is kept if the player closes the letter and opens it again; only E resets it.
- **Edited, `Assets/InventoryInspection.cs`:** inspecting the item called "Clue Letter" now shows the maze, with the hint `W A S D Move / E Restart / ESC Close`. While the maze is open, W/A/S/D move the puzzle player instead of rotating the item, and Esc closes it.
- **Scene:** the maze component adds itself to the Inventory System object at runtime. I didn't edit the scene file because the Unity editor was open.
- **Pause:** player movement, the camera, pickups and the inventory bar already pause during inspection, so they also pause while the maze is open.

**Missing artwork:** the four border images (`orca.png`, `gazelle.png`, `iguana.png`, `panther.png`) aren't in the repo, so the frame draws black squares, like the sketch does before its images load. To use the real art, add a `ClueMinigame` component to the Inventory System object and assign the four textures in its `borderTiles` field. The sketch's `Map.png` is loaded but never drawn, so I left it out.

I ran a solver on the board layout and it can be finished.

ui.content:
I've hooked the four animal tiles up to the maze's border. Nothing has been tested in Unity yet, because the editor hasn't picked up the changes.

- **Import settings:** I created `.meta` files for `Orca_tile_mono.png`, `Gazelle_tile_mono.png`, `Iguana_tile_mono.png` and `Panther_tile_mono.png`. Unity hadn't imported these files yet. They import as single sprites with mipmaps on, so the 260 px images stay clean when shrunk to border-tile size.
- **Scene:** `Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity` now has a `ClueMinigame` component on the Inventory System object. Its `borderTiles` lists orca, gazelle, iguana, panther, the same order the sketch cycles them around the frame.

When you switch back to Unity, it imports the PNGs and reloads the scene. If it asks about the scene being changed outside the editor, choose **Reload**. If you save the open scene over it instead, the component is lost and the border goes back to black squares.

content.text:
I've hooked the four animal tiles up to the maze's border. Nothing has been tested in Unity yet, because the editor hasn't picked up the changes.

- **Import settings:** I created `.meta` files for `Orca_tile_mono.png`, `Gazelle_tile_mono.png`, `Iguana_tile_mono.png` and `Panther_tile_mono.png`. Unity hadn't imported these files yet. They import as single sprites with mipmaps on, so the 260 px images stay clean when shrunk to border-tile size.
- **Scene:** `Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity` now has a `ClueMinigame` component on the Inventory System object. Its `borderTiles` lists orca, gazelle, iguana, panther, the same order the sketch cycles them around the frame.

When you switch back to Unity, it imports the PNGs and reloads the scene. If it asks about the scene being changed outside the editor, choose **Reload**. If you save the open scene over it instead, the component is lost and the border goes back to black squares.

ui.content:
I've rewritten `Assets/ClueMinigame.cs` with all three changes. It compiles cleanly against the project's Unity assemblies, but I haven't played it in the editor. I tuned the board settings with a JavaScript copy of the generator, not in Unity.

1. **20×20 map:** the board is now 20×20 inside a 22-tile frame of the animal tiles. Tiles are drawn at 35 px, so the texture stays about the same size as before. The win screen keeps its original proportions.
2. **Random but solvable:** each new board first picks a target for each colour, each one 10–18 cells from the last. It then cuts a clear path from the centre through all seven targets. That path is never filled in, so every board can be finished.
   - About 65% of the other cells become tiles. Most take the colour of their nearest target, so each colour sits in its own patch and you have to cross the map. 15% get a random colour.
3. **Harder:**
   - **One step per key press:** holding a key no longer keeps moving you. Bumping into a wrong colour doesn't use a step.
   - **Step limit:** the generator searches for a short route and allows that length plus 10% (at least 3 extra). "Steps left" shows under the board, and reaching zero shows "Out of steps".
   - **Dead ends:** the rule is unchanged that any tile of the next colour counts. But clearing the wrong one can cut you off from every tile of the following colour. The game spots this and shows "Dead end".
   - **Test result:** the best route on a typical board is about 40 steps, against about 15 in the original. Always taking the nearest tile of the next colour stayed within the limit on only about half the boards I tested.

Controls: W/A/S/D to step, E to retry the same board, R for a new board, Esc to close. Progress is kept if you close the letter. The win text "Fell, Jerk, Thief" is unchanged.

ui.content:
The Clue Letter now uses `Letter_screen`, and the inspect screen draws the minigame on top of that letter. The scripts compile cleanly, but Unity hasn't imported the new image yet, so I haven't seen it in game.

- **Sprite swap:** in `SampleScene.unity`, the Clue Letter's sprite is now `Letter_screen`. I also pointed the unused `ClueLetter.mat` at the new image, so nothing in the project uses the old `ClueLetter.png` any more.
- **Import settings:** I created `Letter_screen.png.meta` because Unity hadn't imported the file yet. It uses nearest-neighbour filtering and no compression to keep the pixel art sharp, with the pivot at the bottom centre like the old letter. At 300 pixels per unit it stands 1.28 × 0.8 world units, the same width as the old letter. Change Pixels Per Unit on the image if you want it bigger or smaller.
- **Letter behind the minigame:** when the player inspects the letter, the letter fills the same space an inspected item normally does. The board sits on the blank part of the paper, which I found by scanning the image's pixels.
  - "Steps left" is now written to the right of the board in the letter's dark brown, so it reads like handwriting.
  - The win, out-of-steps and dead-end screens cover only the board, so the letter stays visible around them.
  - The letter image is taken from the picked-up item, so no extra setup is needed.
  - The code changes are in `Assets/ClueMinigame.cs`, plus one line in `Assets/InventoryInspection.cs`.

**Smaller tiles:** the board now has to fit inside the paper, so it's about 30% smaller on screen than before. At a 1280×720 window each tile is roughly 16 px. If that's too small to read, I can enlarge the letter or shrink the board's frame.

When you switch back to Unity, it will import the image and reload the scene. If it asks about the scene changing outside the editor, choose **Reload**.

content.text:
The Clue Letter now uses `Letter_screen`, and the inspect screen draws the minigame on top of that letter. The scripts compile cleanly, but Unity hasn't imported the new image yet, so I haven't seen it in game.

- **Sprite swap:** in `SampleScene.unity`, the Clue Letter's sprite is now `Letter_screen`. I also pointed the unused `ClueLetter.mat` at the new image, so nothing in the project uses the old `ClueLetter.png` any more.
- **Import settings:** I created `Letter_screen.png.meta` because Unity hadn't imported the file yet. It uses nearest-neighbour filtering and no compression to keep the pixel art sharp, with the pivot at the bottom centre like the old letter. At 300 pixels per unit it stands 1.28 × 0.8 world units, the same width as the old letter. Change Pixels Per Unit on the image if you want it bigger or smaller.
- **Letter behind the minigame:** when the player inspects the letter, the letter fills the same space an inspected item normally does. The board sits on the blank part of the paper, which I found by scanning the image's pixels.
  - "Steps left" is now written to the right of the board in the letter's dark brown, so it reads like handwriting.
  - The win, out-of-steps and dead-end screens cover only the board, so the letter stays visible around them.
  - The letter image is taken from the picked-up item, so no extra setup is needed.
  - The code changes are in `Assets/ClueMinigame.cs`, plus one line in `Assets/InventoryInspection.cs`.

**Smaller tiles:** the board now has to fit inside the paper, so it's about 30% smaller on screen than before. At a 1280×720 window each tile is roughly 16 px. If that's too small to read, I can enlarge the letter or shrink the board's frame.

When you switch back to Unity, it will import the image and reload the scene. If it asks about the scene changing outside the editor, choose **Reload**.

**Warning:** if you save the scene before doing either of these, Unity will write `ClueLetter` back into the file and overwrite the fix.
